chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the *salam* (advance payment for goods) in animals. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'What is your view if I were to make *salam* for known years, or something known from the slaves, so I give him less than his stipulation, and above it by the agreement of their own selves?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الرَّقِيق: Slaves: Plural of slave, indicating human beings owned as property, historically used in trade contracts.
key_terms.السَّلَم: Salam: A forward contract where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered at a specified future date.
key_terms.الْحَيَوَان: Animals: Livestock or beasts of burden, often used as the subject of salam contracts.
key_terms.بِطِيبَةِ أَنْفُسٍ: By the agreement of their own selves: A phrase indicating mutual consent and goodwill, often used to describe voluntary acceptance of terms or amounts.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on advance payment contracts (salam) for animals and slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* confirms the validity of *salam* in livestock and slaves, a key commercial mechanism in early Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the principle of *bitibat anfusihim* (by the goodness/contentment of their souls), allowing parties to adjust the delivered quantity or price post-agreement if mutually pleased, thereby emphasizing flexibility and consent over rigid contractual adherence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the submission of the advance payment regarding the animals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if I were to submit an advance payment regarding the known years, or something known from the slaves, so I give him less than his stipulation, and above it by the agreement of their own selves?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of advance payment in buying animals. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’

I then asked him (the Imam) if I can make an advance payment for known years or something known like slaves and I pay more or less than his stipulation with consent and happiness. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
